walkthroughs.body_html:
Biodiversity, Evolution & Disease — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biodiversity, Evolution & Disease brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biodiversity, Evolution & Disease.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: An organism with two different alleles at a locus is:
options: Homozygous
Heterozygous
Hemizygous
Polyploid

mcqs.q: A monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes Aa × Aa gives a phenotypic ratio (dominance) of:
How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
The entire DNA sequence of every individual changes simultaneously.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.
Humans evolved directly from chimpanzees, which is why chimps still exist as a less-evolved version.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
No — humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor; both have evolved from it.

mcqs.q: What actually changes during natural selection in a population?
options: Individual organisms change their own genes to adapt.
The entire DNA sequence of every individual changes simultaneously.
Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.
The frequencies of alleles in the population's gene pool change across generations.
